board_identity: THE DIAMONDEDGE PICK — one pick per game
unified_rule: ONE pick per game: for each slate date, DiamondEdge locks one simple four-analyst rule chosen from strictly prior games in trailing 14/21/28 day windows. Candidate rules follow or fade analyst majorities, unanimous desks, individual analysts and agreeing analyst pairs; rules that do not fire pass the game. The selected rule is chosen by net wins with minimum sample, hit-rate and pick-rate filters, then applied to that date's games without using same-day or future results. The served pick carries the rule, trailing record and plain-English rationale. One 0-5 score + star ladder, one record, graded once per game against finals. `source` is diagnostic only.
score_reference_version: v3.3 (Leon, 2026-07-25: full 1-5 display scale — stars = frozen percentile bands of the unchanged v3.2 continuous score over playable rows: top ~10% -> 5*, next ~25% -> 4*, next ~35% -> 3*, rest playable -> 2*, non-playable -> 1*; BH certification is the separate `certified` boolean, no longer the 5* gate)

star_cutoffs.version: v3.3 (Leon, 2026-07-25: full 1-5 display scale — stars = frozen percentile bands of the unchanged v3.2 continuous score over playable rows: top ~10% -> 5*, next ~25% -> 4*, next ~35% -> 3*, rest playable -> 2*, non-playable -> 1*; BH certification is the separate `certified` boolean, no longer the 5* gate)
star_cutoffs.basis: v3.3 percentile display bands of the (unchanged) v3.2 continuous score over ALL playable rows of the season replay (v4 totals grid + champion_v2 2026 backfill). Frozen ABSOLUTE score thresholds for live serving — recomputed only when the replay payload regenerates (nightly), never per-day. The -EV floor is hard: non-playable rows stay 1* regardless of score. `certified` (BH significance) is a separate boolean — no display band claims certification.
star_cutoffs.bands: v3.3 percentile display bands of the continuous v3.2 score over playable rows: score >= cutoff_5 -> 5* (top ~10%), >= cutoff_4 -> 4* (next ~25%), >= cutoff_3 -> 3* (next ~35%), else 2*; 1* = non-playable (hard -EV floor). `certified` (BH significance) is a separate boolean — no star band claims certification.

score_basis.recipe: logit(p_cal) = logit(p_mkt) + s * (logit(p_our) - logit(p_mkt)); s fit by penalized IRLS with identity prior s~N(1, 1/25), clamped to [0, 1.25]; NO intercept (the layer refuses to learn the trailing window's over/under rate); expanding-window walk-forward fit on the engine's own graded FG-totals rows (2026 replay pre-block + served graded ledger, y = final vs judged line, pushes/voids dropped, strictly date < D); refit per serve date, frozen first-fit-wins; inactive (identity) below 300 rows / 10 graded days
score_basis.scope: v4 model-grid FULL-GAME TOTALS our_prob only — champion-stream picks, spread/ML/F5 rows, the EV-gate math and every score/star band cutoff are untouched; they simply receive the calibrated probability
score_basis.note: SCORE BASIS CHANGE (activation-dated 2026-07-27, forward only): the model grid's served probability passes through a walk-forward market-anchored calibration map fitted on strictly-past graded picks before the (unchanged) EV gate and score pipeline. Locked picks, graded history and every past score/record are NEVER restated. A calibrated row can never flip sides — only its stated conviction changes. This does NOT create edge and no edge is claimed: it makes the confidence number mean what it says.

signals_note: signals are contextual factors aligned with the lean, not causal attribution — the model is market-anchored and its number is not derived from these factors

expanded_band.rule: model-grid rows with the FULL +EV gate (ev >= 0.015, unchanged) and conviction 0.0075 <= |our_prob - market_devig| < 0.010 are playable 2* fills from the activation date forward — the exact measured near-miss band; every adjacent band (conviction 0.0050-0.0075, any EV-gate relaxation) measured as a loser and stays PASS

backtest.window: 2026-03-25..2026-07-23 (walk-forward rows only; one game per day-game, best-EV wall; graded vs settled finals at the row's own executable price)
backtest.note: BACKTEST (would-have) record — NOT a served record. The served expanded-band record accrues from EXPANDED_BAND_START under record.by_star_tier['2_expanded'], separately from core 2*.

expanded_band.rails: expanded_band=true on the pick; REGULAR display stars from the one v3.3 ladder (mostly 2* — no separate display row; record.by_star_tier carries includes_expanded_n per tier); 0.5u stake regardless of display stars; graded separately (record.expanded_band.served_record); a core playable row always beats an expanded row on the same game; history is never retroactively promoted

The 2026-07-27 DERIV_RUNLINE_MARGIN_REPORT verdict was BLOCKED (prereg K1: margin fitness gate failed — no home-field advantage in the engine; and every declared arm, including the no-sim control, lost to the de-vigged market on Brier), so lean_only stands. analysts.name: VEGA · The Price
analysts.persona_line: The number is the evidence, so I grade the market and nothing else: where it opened, how far it moved, how much the books disagree and what the two sides actually cost.
analysts.engine: analyst_v2/vega — a published linear formula over the market structure slice ONLY, box-constrained to each lever's declared direction, trained 2025-01-01 -> 2026-06-30. Feature isolation is enforced in code by analyst_v2.slices.FeatureGate: no two analysts share a single fitted column.
analysts.conviction_basis: a logistic residual on logit(de-vigged market probability) with the market coefficient pinned to 1, so the number is a DISAGREEMENT with the price, not a recalibration of it
analysts.note: VEGA is the ONLY analyst for which the market is a model input. It is also the only one that prices a PROBABILITY rather than projecting a total: its model is a residual on logit(de-vigged market probability), which is what a market reader actually does.

analysts.name: ATLAS · The Conditions
analysts.persona_line: Runs are a physical event, so I grade the place and the man behind the plate: the park's run factor, its altitude and roof, day or night, and how many runs this umpire's games actually produce.
analysts.engine: analyst_v2/atlas — a published linear formula over the environment slice ONLY, box-constrained to each lever's declared direction, trained 2025-01-01 -> 2026-06-30. Feature isolation is enforced in code by analyst_v2.slices.FeatureGate: no two analysts share a single fitted column.
analysts.conviction_basis: Phi(delta / sigma) where sigma is the analyst's own TRAIN residual standard deviation — a stated spread, not a walk-forward calibration map
analysts.note: WEATHER IS NOT IN THIS SLICE AND THAT IS A DATA FACT, NOT A CHOICE: wx_* fill is 0.356 in 2025 and 0.006 in 2026, and what exists is ERA5 proxy_ablation which house policy excludes from every clean variant. ATLAS's environment is park + altitude + roof + day/night + umpire run tendency. If a real forward weather feed ever lands, wx_* is the first thing that belongs here.

analysts.name: NOVA · The Bats
analysts.persona_line: Runs come from bats, so I grade the hitters and nothing else: the nine names actually posted tonight against the hand they will face, and how the two offenses have actually been scoring.
analysts.engine: analyst_v2/nova — a published linear formula over the run production slice ONLY, box-constrained to each lever's declared direction, trained 2025-01-01 -> 2026-06-30. Feature isolation is enforced in code by analyst_v2.slices.FeatureGate: no two analysts share a single fitted column.
analysts.conviction_basis: Phi(delta / sigma) where sigma is the analyst's own TRAIN residual standard deviation — a stated spread, not a walk-forward calibration map
analysts.note: NOVA's lineup-vs-hand feature is computed by the enrich layer against the opposing starter's throwing HAND. A hand is an IDENTITY, not a quality: no measure of how good that pitcher is ever reaches NOVA, and no `sp_*` column is in its slice.

analysts.name: SCOUT · The Arms
analysts.persona_line: Runs come from bad pitching, so I grade the arms and nothing else: the two starters who open the game and the bullpens behind them — weak staffs mean runs, and I lean over.
analysts.engine: analyst_v2/scout — a published linear formula over the run prevention slice ONLY, box-constrained to each lever's declared direction, trained 2025-01-01 -> 2026-06-30. Feature isolation is enforced in code by analyst_v2.slices.FeatureGate: no two analysts share a single fitted column.
analysts.conviction_basis: Phi(delta / sigma) where sigma is the analyst's own TRAIN residual standard deviation — a stated spread, not a walk-forward calibration map

analyst_desk_spec.analysts_source_note: EVERY per-game analyst cell, on every board, comes from analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date(date) — the published chief contract over a write-once board — and from nothing else. The four engines that used to back these names (champion_v2 for VEGA, the Monte Carlo simulator for ATLAS, the v4 model grid for NOVA, the simple-8 fundamentals stream for SCOUT) were dismantled on 2026-07-31 and are not read anywhere in this path. Anything consuming this payload should learn the four channels — arms / bats / conditions / price — and nothing about the previous architecture.
analyst_desk_spec.consensus_spread_note: THE ANALYST CONSENSUS IS TOTALS-ONLY. Every v2 read is scope=full_game, bet_type=total — not one of the four produces a run-line call, so every voice here is null and the state is PENDING, permanently and by design. This dimension used to attribute a margin side to ATLAS (from the simulator's joint margin distribution) and to NOVA (from the run-line lean stream). Those were the DISMANTLED engines that used to carry those names; the v2 ATLAS reads the conditions and the v2 NOVA reads the bats, and neither has anything to say about a margin. The key is kept at null rather than removed so nothing downstream changes shape. THE RUN-LINE CALL ITSELF DID NOT GO ANYWHERE: it is served at games[].diamondedge.spread_call, attributed to its actual producers.

retired_coverage_fields.note: FORCED COVERAGE IS RETIRED (2026-07-31). It manufactured a fallback read for whichever DISMANTLED engine had frozen nothing on a game. The v2 stream files a read or files none, and an unfiled seat is served empty. The fields survive at their dead values for shape stability and are dropped from history cards; record.coverage is the frozen ledger of the closed mechanism.

analyst_desk_spec.per_game_fields: SOURCE (REPOINTED 2026-07-31): every per-game analyst cell comes from analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date(date) — the published chief contract over a WRITE-ONCE board — and from nothing else. Each entry stamps source:'analyst_v2_stream'. games[].analysts = [{key, name, persona_line, slice_title, channel, source, side (over|under|null), p_over, conviction (0-1, P(stated side)), conviction_calibrated (FALSE for all four — neither v2 conviction is a walk-forward calibration map; see each analyst's conviction_basis), locked, wall, vs_line, vs_line_is_pregame_line, has_row, take, take_kind}] — ALWAYS all four SEATS, in `order`. null side + has_row=false means THE v2 STREAM FILED NO READ on this game (its T-3h feature frame did not exist — no posted lineup, no umpire, or no consensus total). That seat is served EMPTY and is never backfilled from another model. `locked` is true whenever a read exists, because the board is write-once and a written read can never move again. ANALYST VOICES: `take` is a 1-2 sentence line in the persona's voice rendered FROM THAT ANALYST'S OWN v2 READ ROW (analyst_takes.V2_TEMPLATES — deterministic per analyst x game, byte-stable across regenerations); every number in a take is validator-checked to exist in that row — nothing fabricated, ever. A take never names a lever; the levers are rendered structurally at analysts_v2[].top_drivers. take_kind is standard | dissent (the lone voice against >= 2 opposing reads argues back) | no_read. LIVE ATLAS (2026-07-30): on LIVE games the atlas entry gains {live_p_over, live_state_note, as_of} — the certified conditional simulator re-pricing P(over the pregame line) from the actual game state, ONLY inside its certified fitness buckets (v4/serve/live_atlas.py); outside them live_p_over is null and the note says the desk is watching. DISPLAY ONLY, forever: never graded, never a bet, never touches any record, and flagged live_is_this_analysts_read:false — it is the in-game conditional engine, NOT the v2 ATLAS read beside it. games[].consensus = {source, n_over, n_under, n_no_read, state UNANIMOUS|MAJORITY|SPLIT|PENDING, majority_side, spread: {n_home, n_away, n_no_read, state, majority_side, voices, note, run_line_call_lives_at}} — UNANIMOUS requires all FOUR to agree; MAJORITY is a strict majority of those with reads; SPLIT is a tie of reads; PENDING is no reads. THE SPREAD DIMENSION IS PERMANENTLY EMPTY: the v2 stream is totals-only (every read is scope=full_game, bet_type=total) so no analyst has a margin view, all four voices are null and the state is PENDING by design. It used to attribute a margin side to ATLAS (the simulator's joint margin) and to NOVA (the run-line lean stream) — those were the DISMANTLED engines that carried those names. The run-line call itself is unchanged and lives at games[].diamondedge.spread_call, attributed to its actual producers (run_line_stream / margin_simulator), with voices_are_not_analysts:true. vs_line is the EXACT line that read was priced against — render it as 'ATLAS: OVER 8.5 (priced vs 8.5)' — and vs_line_is_pregame_line (bool|null) states it against the LOCKED pregame line. FORCED COVERAGE IS RETIRED (2026-07-31). The four fields coverage_expanded / coverage_kind / coverage_activation / low_conviction survive at false|null for shape stability and can never be set again: the mechanism manufactured a fallback read for whichever DISMANTLED engine had frozen nothing on a game, and there is no such thing on the v2 stream. payload.board_coverage now MEASURES how much of the board was read (n_no_reads, n_games_fully_read, n_coverage_reads==0) instead of asserting a full board. record.coverage is the frozen ledger of the closed mechanism, stamped closed:true and describes_previous_analysts:true, and never merged into any analyst's record. games[].pregame_line = {total, total_price_over, total_price_under, run_line, run_line_price_home, run_line_price_away, book, captured_at, wall, locked_at, is_locked, total_open, total_move, p_over_devig, n_books, first_captured_at, source, note} | null — the market state at the last wall before first pitch, WRITE-ONCE and immutable from the moment locked_at is stamped. games[].line_now = {total, pregame_total_compared, total_price_over, total_price_under, book(null), comparison_basis('book_consensus_median'), same_basis:true, same_book_check {book, pregame_total, total, move, total_price_over, total_price_under} | null, n_books, as_of, source, market:'full_game_total', moved_vs_pregame, move, max_plausible_move, display_only:true, note} | null — the CURRENT read of the SAME full-game pregame totals market the locked line came from, so a pregame move never mutates the locked line. FOUR RAILS the frontend can rely on: (1) it is ALWAYS the same market — in-play/remaining-runs totals are never a source; (2) it is NULL for any game that has started (after first pitch there is no pregame market to compare to — render the locked line alone); (3) books are NEVER mixed and the headline ALWAYS reconciles with what is on screen: both sides are the same consensus-median basis, so `move` is exactly `line_now.total - pregame_line.total` and `pregame_total_compared` always equals `pregame_line.total` (the anchor book's own move is corroboration only, in `same_book_check`); (4) a comparison implying a move larger than `max_plausible_move` runs, or one where the same-book check moves the opposite way, is refused and logged in payload.line_now_audit, never shipped. So 'MARKET MOVED' should only ever render off a real, plausible, arithmetically-reconciling `move`. games[].live_progress = {status:'in_progress', inning, half, outs, away_score, home_score, runs_so_far, pregame_total, runs_vs_pregame_total, runs_still_needed_for_over, innings_elapsed, pace_runs_per_inning, projected_final_runs, p_hit_now, p_hit_side, p_hit_side_basis, p_hit_certified, p_hit_basis, p_hit_buckets, p_hit_note, live_p_over, as_of, display_only:true, note} | null — p_hit_now is the probability the PREGAME pick still cashes and is populated ONLY inside the live simulator's CERTIFIED buckets (p_hit_certified true); outside them it is null. Every live number is display-only and touches no record. games[].diamondedge = the synthesis frame: the served pick's mirror (side/line/stars/score/price/result/...) + {consensus_state, action PLAY|LEAN|AVOID, action_basis, desk_agreement ALIGNED|MIXED|AGAINST|PENDING, is_bet, action_before_pattern, pattern_downgraded, confidence_rank (3=PLAY,2=LEAN,1=AVOID), rationale_line, pattern, pattern_line, synthesis_config_version, spread_call, predicted_score, desk_call, chief, note}. action_vocabulary.PLAY: A BET WAS SERVED at the product's higher conviction tier (stars >= 3). The +EV gate and the star system made it; the desk did not.
action_vocabulary.LEAN: A BET WAS SERVED at the lower star tier — or a served bet the measured pattern table sized down. A served bet can never display below LEAN.
action_vocabulary.AVOID: NO BET WAS SERVED (pick.status is PASS or VOID). This is the ONLY meaning of AVOID. It is an INVARIANT, asserted in the selftest: the chief can never tell a reader the desk is passing on a bet the engine actually served. AVOID IS NOT SILENCE (2026-08-01): it says nothing cleared the price gate and says nothing at all about what the desk thinks — that is `desk_call`, which is populated on every game including every AVOID.
action_vocabulary.why: the action was a four-way vote; because the served pick's own side is one of the four voices and full coverage (2026-07-30) gave all four a read on every game, three near-coin-flip voices outvoted the picking engine on roughly half of all served bets — so the product served a bet and said 'we're passing' on the same card. Configuration must not drive the recommendation (across 2,972 games no consensus configuration separates from chance), so it no longer does: PLAY vs LEAN is grounded in the star tier, the one confidence ladder here with a measured calibration.
action_vocabulary.where_the_disagreement_went: games[].diamondedge.desk_agreement and .chief.ou_call.desk_agreement = ALIGNED | MIXED | AGAINST | PENDING, plus the rationale_line, which says it in plain English. AGAINST on a served bet is stated as context, never as a veto.
action_vocabulary.this_axis_is_the_bet_only: PLAY / LEAN / AVOID answer ONE question: are we betting this game. They do not, and since 2026-08-01 are not expected to, say anything about what the desk thinks. Read `desk_call` for that.

call_vocabulary.what_this_is: games[].diamondedge.desk_call — THE DESK'S CALL, a directional view on EVERY game. It exists because the product was silent on 13 of 17 games: AVOID means 'no bet cleared the price gate' and says nothing about what the desk thinks, and the desk thinks something about all of them. 'The desk likes the over here, but not at this price' is a decisive, useful, honest thing to say.
call_vocabulary.fields: {state, side over|under, conviction STRONG|CLEAR|SLIGHT, call (e.g. 'CLEAR OVER'), desk_p_over, desk_edge, confidence, line, wall, vote {over, under, no_read}, argument, headline, we_are_betting, bet_action, why_no_bet, call_agrees_with_bet, vote_and_probability_disagree, is_bet:false, staked:false, stake_units:null, playable:false, counts_in_product_record:false, note}

states.CALL_AND_PLAY: the desk has a call AND the bet cleared the price gate at a full star tier — we are on it
states.CALL_AND_LEAN: the desk has a call AND a bet cleared the price gate at the lower tier — we are taking it small
states.CALL_NO_BET: the desk has a call and we are NOT betting it — nothing on this game cleared the price gate. This is the state that used to render as a silent AVOID
states.CALL_NO_GAME: the desk has a call and there is nothing to bet — the game is postponed or has no priced market
states.PENDING: no analyst has filed on this game at any wall yet — the desk has not been dealt the game. The only state with no call, and it is a statement about the feed

call_vocabulary.how_the_side_is_decided: the equal-weight mean of the four analysts' own p_over — the measured house position, since desk_fit's walk-forward refused a fitted combiner (dLL -0.00026, 95% CI [-0.00145, +0.00084]). Each analyst's p_over already carries its own information completeness, so a desk whose voices are thin produces a visibly less convinced call with no extra machinery. The VOTE is reported beside it and is NOT decisive; when the head-count and the probability diverge the row says so.
call_vocabulary.A_CALL_IS_NOT_A_BET: A CALL IS NOT A BET. This is the desk's directional view on the game — what it actually thinks — built from the four analysts' own reads, equal-weighted. It is NEVER staked, it NEVER enters games[].pick, it is never counted in the product record, and it cannot be sized. Whether we are betting this game is a separate question with a separate answer, at `we_are_betting` / `bet_action`, decided by the price gate alone and unchanged by anything here. The graded product remains games[].pick and only games[].pick; the desk's calls are graded in their own ledger, separately, from 2026-08-01.
call_vocabulary.contract: THE DESK-CALL CONTRACT (2026-08-01). WHAT IT IS: a directional view on EVERY game — side, conviction, a probability and a one-line argument — built from the four analysts' own reads, equal-weighted (the measured house position: desk_fit's walk-forward refused a fitted combiner). SERVED AT games[].diamondedge.desk_call. WHAT IT IS NOT: A CALL IS NOT A BET. Whether we are betting a game is decided by the price gate alone and is served, unchanged, at games[].diamondedge.action (PLAY / LEAN / AVOID, where AVOID still means and only means that no bet was served) and at games[].pick. Every call row hard-stamps is_bet=False, staked=False, stake_units=None, playable=False, suggested_units=None, take=False, stars=None and pick_side=None, and those stamps are re-asserted on every write and every read; the module may write only its own three stores and refuses every served board and product ledger by name. THE VOCABULARY, and a reader can never mistake one axis for the other: `desk_call.call` is the CALL (STRONG/CLEAR/SLIGHT + OVER/UNDER), `desk_call.state` fuses both axes (CALL_AND_PLAY / CALL_AND_LEAN / CALL_NO_BET / CALL_NO_GAME / PENDING), `we_are_betting` is the bet in one boolean, and `why_no_bet` names the reason when it is false. GRADING: the graded product remains games[].pick and ONLY games[].pick. The desk's calls are graded in their own append-only ledger, one row per game at its most informed wall, from 2026-08-01, with no units and no ROI because a call has no price.
call_vocabulary.ledger: the desk's calls are graded in their OWN append-only ledger from 2026-08-01, one row per game at its most informed wall, published at record.desk_calls. It carries no units and no ROI because a call has no price. The graded product remains games[].pick and only games[].pick.

analyst_desk_spec.positioning: THE ANALYST DESK (Leon, 2026-07-30): the home screen is a competition — four named analysts, each a real graded engine, call every game; the desk states its consensus and DiamondEdge synthesizes the final frame. SEMANTICS (2026-07-31): the frame follows THE BET, not the vote — a served bet reads PLAY or LEAN by its star tier, a game with no served bet reads AVOID, and the desk's agreement or disagreement is rendered alongside as context. The desk weights its analysts by a nightly rolling 30-day fit of their disagreement with the price (chief.desk_fit), which falls back to equal weighting — and says so — whenever the fit cannot beat equal weighting walk-forward, which is the state today. The underlying pick machinery, every record, and every honesty rail are UNCHANGED underneath.

why: walk-forward, the fitted weights are not distinguishable from equal weighting (delta log-loss -0.00035, 95% CI [-0.00144, +0.00057] on 257 games over 20 days)
rolling_desk_fit.gate: adopt fitted weights only when the trailing window holds >= 300 graded games with >= 100 reads for every analyst AND the walk-forward log-loss improvement over equal weighting has a 95% day-clustered interval strictly better than zero

source.note: the v2 stream's own append-only GRADED LEDGER — the graded half of the write-once board that analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date() serves the desk chief, so the combiner and the chief describe the same desk. Read only; nothing here re-prices or re-grades. Pushes carry no outcome and are dropped, as are games whose analysts were priced at different lines and landed between them.
source.no_longer_read: v4/models/analyst_desk/history.parquet — the walk-forward reconstruction of the PREVIOUS four analysts (VEGA the champion engine, NOVA the v4 grid, ATLAS the simulator, SCOUT the simple-8 fundamentals). Those four were dismantled on 2026-07-31; a weight fitted on their behaviour is not a weight for the analysts it would be applied to. The file is left on disk untouched — nothing is deleted or restated — and is simply never opened by this module.
source.fence: no frame on or before 2026-06-30 — the four models were fitted through that date, so a frame at or before it would be a fit on training data

rolling_desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 257 games and 20 days the log-loss difference is -0.00035 (95% CI [-0.00144, +0.00057]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
rolling_desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
rolling_desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

No analyst shows a positive edge on its own side and none is claimed (the four sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points). What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. Whether it carries edge is a question only the forward record answers.
rolling_desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A BET RULE. It re-fits every night over the trailing 30 days how each analyst's DISAGREEMENT WITH THE PRICE has related to results, scores that fit WALK-FORWARD (fit strictly on days before the day it is scored on, never on the days it is scored on), and compares it to two baselines: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are only ever ADOPTED when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting has an interval strictly better than zero AND the window carries enough reads to fit four weights. When it does not — which is the state today — the desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS and this block says so with the numbers, because presenting a fitted weight whose interval straddles the equal-weight baseline is presenting noise as insight. Nothing here gates, sizes or grades a bet: the +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet, and the combined probability is display only, graded nowhere.

constants.chief_note: THE CHIEF (Leon, 2026-07-30; SEMANTICS REWRITTEN 2026-07-31): DiamondEdge's own PREGAME synthesis — the O/U call, the run-line call and the predicted final score, all against the LOCKED pregame line, with a rationale grounded in the MEASURED tables. THE COHERENCE RULE (the 2026-07-31 fix): when the engine SERVED A BET, the chief's O/U call IS that bet — same side, same number — and the action can never be AVOID. AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served. The desk's disagreement with a served bet is real and is stated (desk_agreement + the rationale line), but it is stated as CONTEXT, never as 'we're passing' on a bet we are actually making. The chief remains PRESENTATION and ROUTING ONLY: the measured pattern table can change the language and move a displayed action DOWN one rung, never up, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and on a served bet the ladder bottoms out at LEAN. Betting stays with the +EV gate and the star system, exactly as before. predicted_score and desk_combined are display predictions, graded nowhere.
constants.ou_call_note: side IS the served bet whenever one was served (side_basis=served_bet); it falls back to the desk's own majority lean only when nothing was served, and a lean is never a bet.
constants.coherence_note: THE BET IS `the_bet` and nothing else on this card is a bet. The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and ATLAS's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

display_layer.what: the adaptive desk — one strategy locked per date from strictly-prior graded history, applied to that date's games. This is the board and the headline record.

supplemental.what: a pick Leon adds by hand from the expanded engine (v2, in shadow), on a game the desk did NOT pick, before first pitch. It FILLS, it never overrides: a supplemental row for a game that already has a served pick, or for a game that has started, is REFUSED and the refusal is published.
supplemental.write_once: admitted once, frozen at that instant into state/supplemental_served.jsonl, replayed from there on every later build, and hash-pinned with the rest of the archive
supplemental.counted: in record.headline, in the day's record and in record.by_source, on its own source line — it was served pregame at a real price, so it is a real pick, and it is never blended into the desk's own line

withdrawal.what: Leon may SUPERSEDE a still-PREGAME served pick, so the board serves that game as a PASS instead. It is refused outright once the game is inside the pregame margin: a standing offer may be taken off the board, a live position may not.
withdrawal.never_an_edit: nothing is rewritten and nothing is deleted. The original row is archived verbatim in state/superseded_picks_<date>.jsonl with what superseded it, who authorised it and when — a second dated fact laid on top of the first, not a change to it
withdrawal.write_once: applied once, first application wins forever, and replayed clocklessly on every later build — a rebuild can no more resurrect a withdrawn pick than it can drop a served one
withdrawal.counted: in NO record. The game was never decided, so it leaves the day's denominator rather than entering it as a win or a loss — which is only honest because the gate refuses any withdrawal on a game that has started

archive_layer.note: The ARCHIVE layer holds every pick the older engines ever served. It is append-only and hash-pinned per day. It is NOT the board: since 2026-08-02 the board is the adaptive desk (the DISPLAY layer). The archive's job is to prove history was never rewritten.

premium.note: Non-premium clients read the PUBLIC payload variant, where every premium field is ABSENT (not null, not masked) on any game carrying a live pick, and every free-text field that could name a side is replaced with the teaser. The record, the number of calls the desk made, and the analysts' personality content stay fully public. Nothing in the public variant contains the pick in any recoverable field — desk_policy.leak_scan() is the rail that proves it.

copy.rule: story / news / desk copy reads ONLY the story_safe blocks. The research_only blocks keep every measurement, sample and interval they have always carried — they are for the Research surface, which reframes a null as 'we tested this, the market prices it, so we bet elsewhere'. No story-safe field may carry null-finding language, and nothing in the payload ranks a research block onto the record or desk surfaces: record.headline is the only product record.

desk_policy.summary: ARCHIVE vs DISPLAY. The write-once served-pick stores are the ARCHIVE layer: append-only, immutable, hash-pinned, never the board. The adaptive desk is the DISPLAY layer: one strategy locked per date from strictly-prior history, and the only thing the site shows or counts. The two populations disagree by design from 2026-08-02; each is reconciled against its OWN ledger, never against the other.

premium_spec.note: Non-premium clients read the PUBLIC payload variant, where every premium field is ABSENT (not null, not masked) on any game carrying a live pick, and every free-text field that could name a side is replaced with the teaser. The record, the number of calls the desk made, and the analysts' personality content stay fully public. Nothing in the public variant contains the pick in any recoverable field — desk_policy.leak_scan() is the rail that proves it.
public_by_contract: record.desk_calls (the COUNT of calls, never their directions)
premium_by_contract: games[].pick.side / line / vegas_line / price / stars / score / our_prob / p_over / ev / suggested_units / signals
games[].diamondedge.* directional fields and the chief block
games[].analysts[].side / take / any prose naming a side

vega.title: THE PRICE
vega.thesis: The number is the evidence, so I grade the market and nothing else: where it opened, how far it moved, how much the books disagree and what the two sides actually cost.
vega.note: VEGA is the ONLY analyst for which the market is a model input. It is also the only one that prices a PROBABILITY rather than projecting a total: its model is a residual on logit(de-vigged market probability), which is what a market reader actually does.
vega.formula: logit(p_over) = logit(p_market) + -0.0542 +0.0000*z[line_move] +0.0000*z[move_pace] -0.0030*z[time_since_move] +0.1270*z[book_disagreement] -0.0494*z[price_dispersion] +0.0169*z[sharp_gap] +0.0263*z[n_books] -0.0664*z[stale_gap]   ;   side = over if p_over > p_market else under

atlas.title: THE CONDITIONS
atlas.thesis: Runs are a physical event, so I grade the place and the man behind the plate: the park's run factor, its altitude and roof, day or night, and how many runs this umpire's games actually produce.
atlas.note: WEATHER IS NOT IN THIS SLICE AND THAT IS A DATA FACT, NOT A CHOICE: wx_* fill is 0.356 in 2025 and 0.006 in 2026, and what exists is ERA5 proxy_ablation which house policy excludes from every clean variant. ATLAS's environment is park + altitude + roof + day/night + umpire run tendency. If a real forward weather feed ever lands, wx_* is the first thing that belongs here.
atlas.formula: delta_runs = (+0.2723*z[park_run_factor] +0.2801*z[park_altitude] -0.1607*z[park_roof] +0.0000*z[is_night] +0.0970*z[ump_runs] -0.0321*z[ump_strikeouts] +0.0000*z[ump_walks]) - -0.0044   ;   p_over = Phi(delta / 4.537)   ;   side = over if delta > 0 else under   ;   projected total shown = posted line + delta   [context-free absolute projection, diagnostic only: mu_absolute = 8.9160 + the same linear term]

nova.title: THE BATS
nova.thesis: Runs come from bats, so I grade the hitters and nothing else: the nine names actually posted tonight against the hand they will face, and how the two offenses have actually been scoring.
nova.note: NOVA's lineup-vs-hand feature is computed by the enrich layer against the opposing starter's throwing HAND. A hand is an IDENTITY, not a quality: no measure of how good that pitcher is ever reaches NOVA, and no `sp_*` column is in its slice.
nova.formula: delta_runs = (+0.0000*z[bats_vs_hand] +0.0000*z[bats_top5_vs_hand] +0.0000*z[bats_woba] +0.1977*z[bats_top5_woba] +0.2454*z[bats_power] +0.0000*z[bats_onbase] +0.0000*z[bats_scoring_form] +0.0000*z[bats_strikeouts] -0.0379*z[bats_lineups_known]) - 0.0156   ;   p_over = Phi(delta / 4.549)   ;   side = over if delta > 0 else under   ;   projected total shown = posted line + delta   [context-free absolute projection, diagnostic only: mu_absolute = 8.9160 + the same linear term]

scout.title: THE ARMS
scout.thesis: Runs come from bad pitching, so I grade the arms and nothing else: the two starters who open the game and the bullpens behind them — weak staffs mean runs, and I lean over.
scout.formula: delta_runs = (+0.0000*z[sp_fip] +0.1631*z[sp_contact_quality] +0.0324*z[sp_worst_contact_quality] +0.1385*z[sp_recent_form] +0.0000*z[sp_worst_recent_form] -0.0752*z[sp_length] -0.1031*z[sp_groundballs] -0.0427*z[sp_rest] +0.2010*z[pen_era] +0.0000*z[pen_worst_era] +0.0000*z[pen_workload] +0.0000*z[pen_worst_workload] +0.0000*z[pen_back_to_back] +0.0000*z[pen_closer_available]) - 0.0316   ;   p_over = Phi(delta / 4.546)   ;   side = over if delta > 0 else under   ;   projected total shown = posted line + delta   [context-free absolute projection, diagnostic only: mu_absolute = 8.9160 + the same linear term]

analyst_v2_spec.chief_contract: THE ANALYST-STREAM CONTRACT (v2, 2026-07-31) — what the desk chief may rely on. SOURCE: v4/serve/analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date(date) -> {game_pk: {analyst_key: read}}, read-only over the write-once board at v4/serve/state/analyst_v2_board.json. GUARANTEES: (1) at most ONE read per (date, game_pk, analyst), written once and never restated — a key already on the board is skipped, not overwritten; (2) every read carries `pick_side` in {over, under} (a read with no side is never written), `p_over` in (0,1), `market_line`, `p_mkt_over` and `edge_vs_market`; (3) the three CHANNEL analysts (scout/nova/atlas) additionally carry `delta_runs` (their signal in runs, positive = over), `center_used` (the strictly-prior trailing centre that delta is measured against), `conviction_runs` = |delta_runs|, `mu_shown` = market_line + delta_runs (the total that analyst projects for THIS game, coherent with the line by construction) and `mu_absolute` (its context-free projection, diagnostic only); VEGA carries `delta_runs`: null because it prices a probability, and its signal is `edge_vs_market`; (4) `top_drivers` is the three levers contributing most to that read, each with its z, its beta and its contribution IN RUNS — safe to render verbatim; (5) `basis` is 'reconstructed_oos' or 'live' and `trained_through` is the training fence, so the chief can weight by evidence type; (6) `is_bet` is ALWAYS false — these are reads, and the served product pick is not built from them. DECORRELATION: the four slices are disjoint and enforced by analyst_v2.slices.FeatureGate, so the chief may treat the four reads as carrying independent information about different causal channels — that is the design property a combiner should exploit. STABILITY: adding a field is allowed; removing or renaming one is a contract break and must be announced.
analyst_v2_spec.wall_contract: THE PER-WALL ANALYST CONTRACT (2026-07-31). SOURCE: v4/serve/analyst_v2_walls.reads_for_wall(date, wall) and timeline_for_date(date), read-only over a WRITE-ONCE store at v4/serve/state/analyst_v2_wall_board.json. GUARANTEES: (1) at most ONE row per (date, game_pk, analyst, wall), written once and never restated; (2) the T-3h wall is NOT in this store — it is owned by analyst_v2_stream's board, which record.analysts is graded from, and reads_for_wall delegates to it so there is exactly one T-3h read per game; (3) EVERY ANALYST FILES A READ WITH A SIDE ON EVERY GAME THAT HAS A DECISION ROW AND A POSTED TOTAL AT THAT WALL (2026-08-01). The evidence floor that used to empty a seat on thin inputs is retired: a lever whose information has not landed takes its NEUTRAL value, contributes exactly 0.00 runs to the deviation, and the analyst files on the rest of its slice. The only remaining empty seat is `no_market` — no posted total, so there is no number to have an opinion about, and it still carries a `reason_code` and a sentence; (4) every read publishes `information_completeness` (the share of the wall model's own |beta| mass genuinely read), `completeness_tier`, `levers_neutral_filled`, `completeness_note` and `confidence_scale` = sqrt(completeness), and its probability is scaled by that — so a read built on less information carries LESS CONVICTION, not the same conviction with a caveat. At completeness 1 the scale is exactly 1 and the read is bit-for-bit the fully-informed one; (5) `top_drivers` NEVER contains a lever that was not read, so no read can cite information it did not have — that lock is UNCHANGED and is what keeps this from being FORCED COVERAGE, WHICH REMAINS RETIRED and cannot be produced by this module; (6) every row carries `wall`, `in_wall_window`, `basis` (live_wall / reconstructed_wall), `information_read`, `information_missing`, `information_not_yet_possible`, `lineup_posted`, `umpire_assigned` and `starters_announced`; (7) `is_bet` is ALWAYS false and nothing here touches games[].pick, record.headline_champion_v2 or record.analysts. THE MODELS: one fit per (analyst, wall) over exactly the levers whose information exists at that wall, fenced at 2026-06-30 like every other analyst model. The T-3h wall fit reproduces the SHIPPED T-3h artifact to 1e-9, which is what proves this is the same engine walked back through the day rather than a second one.

market.label: the posted number
market.reads: the total the books are hanging, and how far it has moved since it opened

venue.label: the ballpark and the time of day
venue.reads: the park's run factor, its altitude, whether it is covered, and whether the game is played in daylight — all of it fixed by the schedule days in advance

umpire.label: the plate umpire
umpire.reads: who is working the plate and how many runs, strikeouts and walks his games actually produce

probables.label: the announced starting pitchers
probables.reads: the two starters MLB has announced, and everything their game logs and Statcast say about them

bullpen.label: the two bullpens
bullpen.reads: what each bullpen has thrown over the last three days, who is unavailable, and how good the pen is

team_offense.label: how the two offences have been scoring
team_offense.reads: team batting over the last fifteen and thirty games — known long before anybody posts a lineup card

projected_lineup.label: the projected lineup card
projected_lineup.reads: the lineup as it is PROJECTED at this wall — a real pregame artifact, snapshotted at the wall, and not the same thing as the card the manager actually posts

posted_lineup.label: the nine names actually posted
posted_lineup.reads: the nine names the manager actually posted tonight and the hand each of them will face — which does not exist before the lineups go up, at any price

completeness.note: EVERY ANALYST FILES ON EVERY GAME AT EVERY WALL (2026-08-01). A lever whose information has not landed takes its NEUTRAL value and contributes exactly zero to the deviation; the read stands on the rest of the slice. What used to be an evidence FLOOR is now a MEASUREMENT: `information_completeness` is the share of the model's own |beta| mass that was genuinely read, it is published on every read, and the read's confidence is scaled by its square root — so a read built on less information is a less confident read rather than an absent one. A neutral-filled lever still cannot be cited, by `citable_drivers` and by the take library's information gate, which is what keeps this from being the retired forced-coverage mechanism in a new coat.

reason_codes.no_frame: no decision row exists for this game at this wall yet — the wall has not been crossed or the collector has not reached it
reason_codes.no_market: no consensus total is posted for this game at this wall, so there is no number to price against
reason_codes.structural: the information this analyst reads does not exist at this wall for any game
reason_codes.missing_inputs: the information this analyst reads has not landed for this game yet
reason_codes.thin_evidence: RETIRED 2026-08-01 — too little of this analyst's own slice was populated for this game. It no longer stops a read: the missing levers take their neutral value, contribute nothing, and the read is filed with its information completeness stated and its conviction reduced accordingly.
reason_codes.no_side: RETIRED 2026-08-01 — this analyst's channel came out exactly neutral. It no longer stops a read: the tie breaks to over, the probability is exactly 0.500 and the completeness is published as 0, so the card shows a side with visibly nothing behind it.

wall_coverage_table.note: WHAT EACH ANALYST CAN READ AT EACH WALL. Exactly one entry here is a structural claim about the sport rather than about the feed: the posted lineup does not exist before T-3h. It is MEASURED, not asserted — across every wall row since 2025-01-01 the fact table's lineup_known flags are 0.0000 at T-24h, T-12h and T-6h and 0.9974 at T-3h and T-1h, and the selftest re-measures it against the parquet on every run. Everything else is probed per game at pricing time, because 'the umpire is usually assigned late' and 'MLB has not named tomorrow's starter' are facts about a particular game, not rules.

analyst_v2_spec.multi_wall: EVERY ANALYST NOW PRICES EVERY WALL FROM T-24h FORWARD. Until 2026-07-31 the four priced a game only where its T-3h frame existed, which on a live evening board left more than half the games with four empty seats for most of the day — a regression against the standing requirement that every game carries a read from every analyst. Each analyst now has ONE MODEL PER WALL, fitted on that wall's own fenced training frame over exactly the levers whose information exists there, and games[].analysts fills each seat from the most informed wall that actually has a read, with the wall stamped on the seat. THE T-3h WALL IS UNCHANGED AND STILL OWNS THE RECORD: the T-3h wall fit reproduces the shipped T-3h artifact to 1e-9, record.analysts is still the T-3h read one row per game, and the per-wall reads are graded in their own ledger and published additively. FORCED COVERAGE IS STILL RETIRED and cannot return through this door: a read is written only when the analyst's own inputs are genuinely populated, a driver whose lever was imputed is stripped before anything can render it, the voice is gated off any sentence claiming information the read did not have, and an analyst below the evidence floor files NOTHING — the seat states why.
analyst_v2_spec.strategy_contract: games[].analysts[].strategy — the LIVE CLAUDE STRATEGY advisory, or absent. SHAPE {strategy_stance ('concur'|'caution'), strategy_caution (bool), strategy_note (one or two sentences, safe to render verbatim), cited_levers[], advisory_only:true, moved_the_pick:false, pick_side_unchanged, note, asof_utc}. WHAT IT IS: a Claude session that reasons about ONE analyst's own slice, its own reads for tonight and its own recent record. WHAT IT IS NOT: it does not and structurally cannot set a side, a probability, a line, a price or a stake — there is no such field in its response schema, the pricing fields are written write-once BEFORE any session runs, and the graded ledger is written from the untouched board row, so a session can never move an analyst's record in either direction. Every number in strategy_note is validated to be derivable from that game's own read row by analyst_takes.validate_take (the same validator the deterministic take-generator uses); a note that invents a number is dropped whole. strategy_caution is DOWNGRADE-ONLY: it may flag a game as less comfortable, never as more.
analyst_v2_spec.predicted_score_contract: games[].diamondedge.predicted_score — ATLAS's projected score. CHANGED 2026-07-31: the two numbers are now per-team EXPECTED RUNS (means), shown to one decimal, and they SUM TO `projected_total` by construction. They used to be per-team MEDIANS, which are integers and therefore collapsed most games onto 4-5, and which summed BELOW the projected total by 0.71 runs on average. SHAPE {away (float, 1dp), home (float, 1dp), source:'ATLAS', p_home_win, wall, projected_total, statistic:'expected_runs', note}. RENDERING: show one decimal — rounding to an integer reintroduces exactly the defect this fixed. It is a DISPLAY prediction, graded nowhere, and it is never a bet.
analyst_v2_spec.fence: TRAINING FENCE: every one of the four analysts is fit strictly on games dated 2025-01-01 through 2026-06-30 inclusive. No model sees a single row dated 2026-07-01 or later — the fence is asserted in dataset.assert_no_post_fence(), re-asserted by the trainer on every matrix it fits, and re-checked against every written artifact by the selftest. The live record for all four analysts begins 2026-07-01 and accrues forward.
analyst_v2_spec.seal_spend: THIS TRAINING WINDOW SPENDS SEALED DATE WINDOWS, KNOWINGLY. The program had sealed the 2024-04-01 -> 2026-04-30 confirmation corpus and the 2026-05-01+ cross-book holdout. The 2025-01-01 -> 2026-06-30 training window runs straight through both, and Leon chose that deliberately in exchange for a clean forward evaluation window that starts the day training ends. CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED: every number computed on the training window is IN-SAMPLE and carries NO evidential weight about future performance. The only honest evidence about these four analysts is the record that accrues from 2026-07-01 forward, on data no model has ever seen.
analyst_v2_spec.what_changed: THE FOUR ANALYSTS WERE RE-ARCHITECTED ON 2026-07-31. They used to be four different ENGINES over essentially the SAME market-anchored feature space, and the measurement showed it: all four sat between 48.6% and 51.0% on their own sides, the profile pass found ZERO measurable specialisms across 357 cells after correction, and no consensus configuration separated from chance across 2,972 games. They are now four THEORIES OF A BASEBALL GAME reading DISJOINT slices of the feature space — run prevention, run production, environment, price — enforced in code by analyst_v2.slices.FeatureGate. All four were retrained on 2025-01-01 -> 2026-06-30 and all four records restart at 2026-07-01. The served pick and the champion product record are untouched by any of it.

definitions.label: The DiamondEdge Pick
definitions.what: The one pick we actually serve on this game: the champion's play if it has one, otherwise the model's best playable lean, otherwise a PASS.
definitions.basis: POPULATION: every (date, game_pk) where the served hybrid produced a graded pick — champion play if present, else the model's best playable lean — exactly one row per game. GRADING: the row's own settled result at the real executable per-side price it was served at, on the line locked at first pitch; pushes return the stake and leave the ROI denominator. HEADLINE COVERS: served picks from 2026-07-20 (the day the hybrid went live) forward only.

definitions.label: Champion engine
definitions.what: The champion engine's own totals play — its frozen pipeline plus the +EV gate at the real per-side price. It only speaks on games where its trigger fires; on every other game it has no view at all.
definitions.basis: POPULATION: every game the champion engine itself rated PLAYABLE and that settled — one row per game (its highest-score playable wall). This is NOT the champion's published headline, which counts one row per game x STREAM at the last decision wall; the two populations are reconciled to a zero residual by champion_headline_residual(). GRADING: champion_v2's own graded ledger, untouched — gate at the median de-vig price, priced and settled at the best executable price at the same line. HEADLINE COVERS: forward paper ledger + live board from 2026-07-02 forward. The 2026-03-27..06-10 rolling-origin rows are a WALK-FORWARD BACKTEST and are reported separately.

definitions.label: V4 model grid
definitions.what: The v4 model grid's best playable totals lean on the game (+EV gate at the real price AND at least 1 point of model-vs-market disagreement).
definitions.basis: POPULATION: every game where the v4 model grid had a playable totals row that settled — one row per game (core playable preferred over an expanded-band row, then highest score). This DELIBERATELY INCLUDES games the champion also played, which record.by_source.model does NOT: by_source counts only the games the model FILLED after the champion passed, so the two numbers differ and neither is wrong. GRADING: the grid's own graded rows — as-of-wall archive where a day has one, else the live graded ledger — at each row's real executable per-side price. HEADLINE COVERS: 2026-07-06 forward (the first day the grid's live ledger graded anything).

definitions.label: Expanded band
definitions.what: The narrow near-miss band: full +EV gate cleared but the model/market disagreement is only 0.75-1.0 points. Live from 2026-07-24, stakes 0.5u, graded on its own.
definitions.basis: POPULATION: v4 model-grid rows that cleared the FULL +EV gate with model-vs-market disagreement of 0.0075-0.010, on games from the 2026-07-24 activation forward — one row per game. A strict SUBSET of model_v4: every expanded pick is also a model_v4 pick. GRADING: same rows, same real prices; staked 0.5u on the weighted line. HEADLINE COVERS: served picks from 2026-07-24 only — the band is never applied retroactively.

definitions.label: Spread stream (run line)
definitions.what: The run-line (±1.5) side per game — a NEW stream, live from 2026-07-27, graded in public from day one, starting 0-0-0. Separate from the totals product in every record.
definitions.basis: POPULATION: every game the run-line stream served from its 2026-07-27 activation forward — one graded row per game (the latest locked wall), stream-stamped rows only. A DIFFERENT MARKET from everything above: it never overlaps, sums with, or competes against any totals record. GRADING: the same board rails as totals — locked at first pitch, graded overnight at the REAL locked per-side run-line price, write-once, pushes returned. HEADLINE COVERS: 2026-07-27 forward only — the stream starts 0-0-0; the pre-pivot spread era (retired 2026-07-07, adjudicated a research NULL) is history, never credit.

definitions.label: Physical run simulator
definitions.what: A fully-physical Monte Carlo of the game — every plate appearance drawn from empirical base-out transition tables tilted to the two lineups, starters, bullpens, park, weather and umpire as of each decision wall (T-24h through T-1h, re-priced as inputs firm up, each wall written once), with home-field advantage on, 20,000 games simulated — priced into P(over the posted total). The lean that grades is the latest wall locked at first pitch. Shown for transparency: on full-game totals it statistically TIES the market (its median lands within ~0.02 runs of the posted line; blend-vs-market p=0.28), so it is a tracked voice, never a bet.
definitions.basis: POPULATION: every game the physical simulator priced from its 2026-07-28 activation forward — ONE graded row per game. The sim re-prices at each decision wall as inputs firm up (T-24h through T-1h from 2026-07-30; T-3h only before that), every wall write-once, and the row that grades is the LATEST wall locked at first pitch (earlier walls settle 'superseded', kept for audit, never counted). Sim-stamped rows from the stream's OWN ledger only. GRADING: the stated lean (the side implied by the sim's P(over) vs the market's) graded against the settled final at the LOCKED posted line, overnight, append-only — but this is a LEAN LEDGER, not a betting record: no units are ever staked, is_bet is false on every row, and stars are hard-capped at 1*. HEADLINE COVERS: 2026-07-28 forward only — the stream starts 0-0-0, and the sim round's backtest (a statistical TIE with the market) is evidence about the engine, never credit.

status_vocabulary.PICK: this strategy would bet the game at the side/line/price shown
status_vocabulary.PASS: this strategy saw the game and declined — `side`/`line` still carry its lean, `reason` says why it is not a bet
status_vocabulary.NO_VIEW: this strategy produced no row for this game at all — stated explicitly, never silently omitted

strategies_spec.per_game_fields: games[].strategies[] = [{key, label, status, is_headline, is_served_source, side, line, vegas_line, price, stars, score, result, lead_time, locked, expanded_band, pass_why, reason}]. Exactly one entry per strategy per game, always all of them, in `order`. games[].pick is UNCHANGED and remains the single served pick; the is_headline entry mirrors it.
strategies_spec.inclusion_bar: A stream is listed only if it is computed every day into a real side/line/price decision AND has its own graded ledger. Closed research fronts (the ~60 tested-and-null mechanisms), spec-only bands, display selections like 'featured', and price-convention variants are NOT strategies and are not here.
strategies_spec.overlap_note: READ THIS BEFORE COMPARING STRATEGIES. (1) THEY OVERLAP: the same game appears in more than one stream — expanded_band is a strict SUBSET of model_v4, and unified is whichever of champion/model_v4 won that game. Their records are NOT additive: do not sum n, units or ROI across strategies, and do not read 'four strategies' as four independent bets. (2) NO POST-HOC PICKING: choosing whichever stream currently looks best is not a strategy — with four overlapping streams on a few dozen graded picks, one of them looks good by construction. The only number that ever described a real bankroll is the served unified pick from its activation date forward. (3) LIVE vs BACKTEST are kept apart on purpose: each strategy's headline n/W-L-P here is its LIVE-SERVED picks only; reconstructed / walk-forward / would-have measurements sit in `backtest`, are labeled, and are never added to the live number. `combined_view` restates the union ONLY because the older published blocks (record.overall, record.by_source) report it — it is not a live record. (4) Sample sizes here are small. None of this is an edge claim.

performance_claim: Adaptive four-analyst selector, measured from strictly-prior trailing windows; no same-day or future result can choose that day's rule.
positioning: THE DIAMONDEDGE PICK (Leon, 2026-07-20): one pick per game, one score, one star ladder, one record. Since 2026-08-02 the public total uses the locked daily four-analyst adaptive strategy: it can follow, fade or pass depending on the trailing pattern evidence. Champion/model streams remain diagnostic.

headline.label: DiamondEdge
sourced_from: ARCHIVE stores (hash-pinned) via the same select_unified rule the board ran at the time — 2026-07-01 .. 2026-08-02
the adaptive desk's write-once ledger — 2026-08-02 onward
headline.basis: every game DiamondEdge served as an official pick, graded at the price and line it was served at, one row per game, across every engine change. Nothing re-graded, nothing restated, and no part of it is a strategy replayed over days it did not actually play.

walk_forward_adaptive_era.no_lookahead_basis: adaptive_desk_strategy.choose_strategy fits each date only on games final BEFORE that date; this holds for every date, including recomputations.
walk_forward_adaptive_era.note: A date is walk-forward if and only if its strategy was stamped into the as-served ledger (v4/serve/state/adaptive_desk_served.jsonl) before that day's first pitch. That store is append-only, first-write-wins per date, and is NOT the selector's own store — which matters, because choose_strategy is write-once per (date, VERSION), so a selector version bump re-derives every past date under the new selector and overwrites the evidence of what was actually served. That is exactly what happened on 2026-08-02: the v20 bump rewrote 80 of 82 dates in one twelve-minute window. Those days still have no look-ahead inside any single day, but the selector itself was developed with their outcomes visible, so they are a REPLAY of the current selector, not a record, and record.headline excludes them. Going forward, choose_strategy(today, write_once=True) runs in the 02:00 PT overnight cycle — about eight hours before first pitch — and the stamp is written then, so the record accrues honestly from that point and survives every future version bump.
