streaks.note: pushes are neutral — they neither extend nor break a streak. `site` runs over the SAME served picks record.headline counts, straight through the engine changeover; each analyst's runs over that analyst's own v2 reads, which are a different and much larger population — the two are never summed.

surfaces.note: record.headline is the DiamondEdge record. Every other stream/strategy record in this payload is a RESEARCH variant: still graded, still honest, still published — and not a product record. Nothing here ranks or features them.

copy_policy.rule: story / news / desk copy reads ONLY the story_safe blocks. The research_only blocks keep every measurement, sample and interval they have always carried — they are for the Research surface, which reframes a null as 'we tested this, the market prices it, so we bet elsewhere'. No story-safe field may carry null-finding language, and nothing in the payload ranks a research block onto the record or desk surfaces: record.headline is the only product record.

adaptive_selector_replay.label: Selector replay — NOT a track record
adaptive_selector_replay.why_not_the_record: these picks were never served. They are what the current selector says it would have chosen on days the champion/model engine was actually on the board. Judging the selector: useful. Quoting it as a record: an advertisement.

diagnostics.note: measurements kept for judging the engines. Nothing here is a track record and nothing here is ever summed into record.headline.

display_layer.what: the adaptive desk — one strategy locked per date from strictly-prior graded history, applied to that date's games. This is the board and the headline record.

supplemental.what: a pick Leon adds by hand from the expanded engine (v2, in shadow), on a game the desk did NOT pick, before first pitch. It FILLS, it never overrides: a supplemental row for a game that already has a served pick, or for a game that has started, is REFUSED and the refusal is published.
supplemental.write_once: admitted once, frozen at that instant into state/supplemental_served.jsonl, replayed from there on every later build, and hash-pinned with the rest of the archive
supplemental.counted: in record.headline, in the day's record and in record.by_source, on its own source line — it was served pregame at a real price, so it is a real pick, and it is never blended into the desk's own line

withdrawal.what: Leon may SUPERSEDE a still-PREGAME served pick, so the board serves that game as a PASS instead. It is refused outright once the game is inside the pregame margin: a standing offer may be taken off the board, a live position may not.
withdrawal.never_an_edit: nothing is rewritten and nothing is deleted. The original row is archived verbatim in state/superseded_picks_<date>.jsonl with what superseded it, who authorised it and when — a second dated fact laid on top of the first, not a change to it
withdrawal.write_once: applied once, first application wins forever, and replayed clocklessly on every later build — a rebuild can no more resurrect a withdrawn pick than it can drop a served one
withdrawal.counted: in NO record. The game was never decided, so it leaves the day's denominator rather than entering it as a win or a loss — which is only honest because the gate refuses any withdrawal on a game that has started

archive_layer.note: The ARCHIVE layer holds every pick the older engines ever served. It is append-only and hash-pinned per day. It is NOT the board: since 2026-08-02 the board is the adaptive desk (the DISPLAY layer). The archive's job is to prove history was never rewritten.

premium.note: Non-premium clients read the PUBLIC payload variant, where every premium field is ABSENT (not null, not masked) on any game carrying a live pick, and every free-text field that could name a side is replaced with the teaser. The record, the number of calls the desk made, and the analysts' personality content stay fully public. Nothing in the public variant contains the pick in any recoverable field — desk_policy.leak_scan() is the rail that proves it.

copy.rule: story / news / desk copy reads ONLY the story_safe blocks. The research_only blocks keep every measurement, sample and interval they have always carried — they are for the Research surface, which reframes a null as 'we tested this, the market prices it, so we bet elsewhere'. No story-safe field may carry null-finding language, and nothing in the payload ranks a research block onto the record or desk surfaces: record.headline is the only product record.

policy.summary: ARCHIVE vs DISPLAY. The write-once served-pick stores are the ARCHIVE layer: append-only, immutable, hash-pinned, never the board. The adaptive desk is the DISPLAY layer: one strategy locked per date from strictly-prior history, and the only thing the site shows or counts. The two populations disagree by design from 2026-08-02; each is reconciled against its OWN ledger, never against the other.

backtest.window: 2026-03-25..2026-07-23 (walk-forward rows only; one game per day-game, best-EV wall; graded vs settled finals at the row's own executable price)
backtest.note: BACKTEST (would-have) record — NOT a served record. The served expanded-band record accrues from EXPANDED_BAND_START under record.by_star_tier['2_expanded'], separately from core 2*.

expanded_band.note: served_record is the ONLY record the expanded band has earned live (starts 0-0-0 at activation); `backtest` is the labeled would-have measurement that justified the band. The two are never merged. DISPLAY (2026-07-25): expanded picks carry regular stars on the one ladder and are counted inside by_star_tier (each tier's includes_expanded_n says how many) — this block is the band's own separate grading, unchanged.

streaks.note: pushes are neutral — they neither extend nor break a streak

insights.basis: honest aggregates over the SAME one-per-game graded unified picks as record.overall — nothing re-graded, no new claims. equity_curve is CUMULATIVE (units_flat = 1u per pick at the row's own executable price; units_weighted = tier-ladder staked, expanded fills 0.5u); by_star_perf uses the current v3.3 display bands over all history; calibration_buckets compare the served side's model probability to the realized win rate (pushes excluded); streaks treat pushes as neutral.

spread_stream.label: Spread stream (run line)
spread_stream.what: The run-line (±1.5) side per game — a NEW stream, live from 2026-07-27, graded in public from day one, starting 0-0-0. Separate from the totals product in every record.

engine.model: residual_spread_v1 (rolling engine full-game spread cells — the same live engine that serves totals; direction only)
engine.basis: unproven spread stream — served as an honest LEAN only. The direction is the live model's read of the run line; the pre-pivot spread machinery was adjudicated NOT deployable (no cell cleared matched baselines + Brier + CLV + monotonicity), and the run-line simulator engine verdict (2026-07-27) came back BLOCKED — the margin fitness gate failed and the de-vigged run-line market beat every declared arm. Nothing here is a bet.
engine.upgrade_path: UPGRADE PATH: a future run-line engine that passes its margin fitness gate with a surviving arm and real economics can flip the stream to sim_pricing (P(cover) from a validated joint margin distribution, +EV gate at real per-side prices, max 2*). The 2026-07-27 DERIV_RUNLINE_MARGIN_REPORT verdict was BLOCKED (prereg K1: margin fitness gate failed — no home-field advantage in the engine; and every declared arm, including the no-sim control, lost to the de-vigged market on Brier), so lean_only stands. The flip is explicit and human-signed (state/spread_engine_mode.json) — never automatic, never regex-parsed off a research report.

spread_stream.note: GRADED LEAN LEDGER — NOT A BETTING RECORD. The spread stream is live in lean_only mode: every game's stated run-line lean is locked at first pitch and graded against the final at the real locked price, in public, from the 2026-07-27 activation forward — but a lean is not a bet, no units are ever suggested, and no edge is claimed. The record starts 0-0-0 and accrues only from days the stream actually served. It is never added to, or compared against, the totals record.
spread_stream.separation: this record counts ONLY stream-stamped run-line rows graded on/after 2026-07-27; it never contains a totals row, and no totals record (overall, by_strategy, live_record, champion) ever contains a spread row — selftested in spread_stream, daily_cycle and unified_model

price_validity.why: run-line results before 2026-07-31 were graded from best-price columns written before the price-validity rule landed. Their two-sided prices imply arbitrage that was never obtainable (5th-percentile overround 0.729), so the ROI and units on those rows are not a measurement of anything. W-L is unaffected; the money is.

sim_stream.label: Physical run simulator
sim_stream.what: A fully-physical Monte Carlo of the game — every plate appearance drawn from empirical base-out transition tables tilted to the two lineups, starters, bullpens, park, weather and umpire as of each decision wall (T-24h through T-1h, re-priced as inputs firm up, each wall written once), with home-field advantage on, 20,000 games simulated — priced into P(over the posted total). The lean that grades is the latest wall locked at first pitch. Shown for transparency: on full-game totals it statistically TIES the market (its median lands within ~0.02 runs of the posted line; blend-vs-market p=0.28), so it is a tracked voice, never a bet.

engine.model: physical Monte Carlo run simulator (v4/models/forecast/monte_carlo_sim s1-s9; HFA ON; 20,000 sims/game, re-priced at every decision wall)
engine.decision_point: every wall T-24h/T-12h/T-6h/T-3h/T-1h — write-once per wall; the latest wall locked at first pitch is what grades

calibration.recipe: walk-forward mean map E[runs] = a + b*mu_raw, last expanding-window fold (prior months only)

evidence.engine_fitness: ENGINE_FIT_PASS (s5 gate 0): variance ratio and skew inside tolerance; the distributional shape is real
evidence.vs_market: primary arm (sim_blend) brier_gap +1.28e-04 vs the de-vigged market, day-clustered bootstrap p=0.279 over n=8412 — a statistical TIE; no declared arm beat the market
evidence.median_vs_line: the calibrated sim's MEDIAN lands within ~0.02 runs of the posted line on average — an independent physical model reproducing Vegas's number
evidence.hfa: s9 home-field module ON (fit on 2018-21 training seasons only)

engine.basis: physics simulator — ties the market, no proven edge
engine.upgrade_path: UPGRADE PATH: if a future engine-vs-market report (v4/models/output/SIM_TOTALS_EDGE_REPORT.md) shows the simulator actually beating the de-vigged market on a declared, walk-forward, BH-controlled test, the stream may flip to a priced mode — and only via an explicit human-signed state file (state/sim_engine_mode.json) written after that report is read. The 2026-07 sim round's verdict was a TIE (primary arm brier_gap +1.28e-04, p=0.279; the market won or tied every declared arm), so transparent_voice stands. The flip is never automatic and never regex-parsed off a research report.

sim_stream.note: GRADED LEAN LEDGER — NOT A BETTING RECORD. The simulator prices every game's posted total from a full physical simulation and states which side its probability implies; it re-prices at each decision wall as inputs firm up (T-24h through T-1h, every wall write-once, never revised), and the lean that grades is the LATEST wall locked at first pitch — one graded row per game, graded against the final in public, from the 2026-07-28 activation forward — but a lean is never a bet, no units are ever staked, and no edge is claimed: the engine's validated result is that it TIES the market. The record starts 0-0-0 and is never added to, or compared against, the totals or spread records.
sim_stream.separation: this record counts ONLY sim-stamped rows from the stream's own ledger (state/sim_graded.jsonl), graded on/after 2026-07-28; it never contains a row from the totals or spread ledgers, and no totals/spread record ever contains a simulator row — the simulator never writes the shared board or the shared graded ledger at all (selftested in sim_stream, daily_cycle and unified_model)

scout_stream.label: Simple-8 fundamentals model
scout_stream.what: Eight numbers a 1990s scout would recognise — both starters' ERAs, both teams' last-30-day batting averages, both bullpens' ERAs, the park's 3-year run factor and the game-time temperature — refit every morning on every settled game since 2022 and applied as an adjustment to the market's own probability at the T-3h wall. Shown for transparency: in the forecast round this exact model statistically LOST to the de-vigged market (brier gap +1.96e-04, p=0.80, n=9,168), so it is a tracked voice, never a bet.

engine.model: simple-8 fundamentals residual model (fundamentals_baseline S1::residual; ridge-logistic on the logit(p_market) offset, lambda=300; walk-forward daily refit on T-3h rows; priced at EVERY wall T-24h/T-12h/T-6h/T-3h/T-1h from 2026-07-30 so no game is ever a no-read)
engine.wall_disclosure: coefficients are fit on T-3h rows (the frozen prereg recipe, unchanged); at earlier walls those same coefficients are applied to that wall's as-of inputs. Each row stamps wall_train_serve_match so the seam is visible per row. SCOUT is a tracked lean, never a bet — nothing here is staked.
engine.refit: expanding-window daily: predict_day(D) trains on every settled game with game_date < D (research store 2022-03-21..2026-07-04 + serve-era store 2026-07-06..)

evidence.vs_market: S1::residual (this exact 8-input offset recipe) brier_gap +1.96e-04 vs the de-vigged market, day-clustered bootstrap p=0.799 over n=9,168 dev games (2022-2026) — the market wins; no declared arm in the family beat it
evidence.family_verdict: all 6 declared fundamentals arms (S1/S2/R x standalone/residual) failed G1; economics never run (prereg forbids monetising a no-gain cell)
evidence.why_this_arm: S1::residual is the closest-to-market arm of the family and the one Leon named for the desk: 8 inputs, interpretable, honest

engine.basis: simple-8 fundamentals model — the market beat it in validation, no edge claimed
engine.upgrade_path: UPGRADE PATH: if a future engine-vs-market report (v4/models/output/SCOUT_TOTALS_EDGE_REPORT.md) shows this model actually beating the de-vigged market on a declared, walk-forward, BH-controlled test, the stream may flip to a priced mode — and only via an explicit human-signed state file (state/scout_engine_mode.json) written after that report is read. The fundamentals round's verdict was an honest null (S1::residual brier_gap +1.96e-04, p=0.799 — the market won every declared arm), so transparent_voice stands. The flip is never automatic and never regex-parsed off a research report.

scout_stream.note: GRADED LEAN LEDGER — NOT A BETTING RECORD. SCOUT prices every game's posted total from eight classic fundamentals and states which side its probability implies; each stated lean is locked when it is computed at the T-3h wall (write-once) and graded against the final in public, from the 2026-07-30 activation forward — but a lean is never a bet, no units are ever staked, no stars are ever awarded, and no edge is claimed: the model's validated result is that the de-vigged market beat it. The record starts 0-0-0 and is never added to, or compared against, the totals or spread records.
scout_stream.separation: this record counts ONLY scout-stamped rows from the stream's own ledger (state/scout_graded.jsonl), graded on/after 2026-07-30; it never contains a row from the totals, spread or simulator ledgers, and no other record ever contains a scout row — the stream never writes the shared board or the shared graded ledger at all (selftested here and in unified_model)

unified.label: The DiamondEdge Pick
unified.what: The one pick we actually serve on this game: the champion's play if it has one, otherwise the model's best playable lean, otherwise a PASS.
unified.basis: POPULATION: every (date, game_pk) where the served hybrid produced a graded pick — champion play if present, else the model's best playable lean — exactly one row per game. GRADING: the row's own settled result at the real executable per-side price it was served at, on the line locked at first pitch; pushes return the stake and leave the ROI denominator. HEADLINE COVERS: served picks from 2026-07-20 (the day the hybrid went live) forward only.
unified.note: This is the product. Everything else on this page is a component or a diagnostic. The pre-activation block is the same rule applied backwards over picks the champion and the model really made — the picks are real, the selection between them is a would-have, and part of it rests on the champion's rolling-origin backtest.

champion.label: Champion engine
champion.what: The champion engine's own totals play — its frozen pipeline plus the +EV gate at the real per-side price. It only speaks on games where its trigger fires; on every other game it has no view at all.

forward_paper_live.what: logged forward in the champion's paper ledger before first pitch

live_board.what: served live on the v4 board and graded that night

repaired_live_day.what: a live day whose board was unstable (2026-07-08 serving bug) and was reconstructed under the fixed pipeline

backtest.label: ROLLING-ORIGIN WALK-FORWARD BACKTEST — the champion's own pipeline replayed on an expanding window. Nothing was served or logged on these days.

rolling_origin_backtest.what: rolling-origin expanding-window WALK-FORWARD BACKTEST of the champion's own pipeline — nothing was served or logged on these days

combined_view.label: PUBLISHED COMBINED (live + reconstructed/backtest) — shown only because the older blocks report it. This is NOT a live record; do not quote it as one.

champion.basis: POPULATION: every game the champion engine itself rated PLAYABLE and that settled — one row per game (its highest-score playable wall). This is NOT the champion's published headline, which counts one row per game x STREAM at the last decision wall; the two populations are reconciled to a zero residual by champion_headline_residual(). GRADING: champion_v2's own graded ledger, untouched — gate at the median de-vig price, priced and settled at the best executable price at the same line. HEADLINE COVERS: forward paper ledger + live board from 2026-07-02 forward. The 2026-03-27..06-10 rolling-origin rows are a WALK-FORWARD BACKTEST and are reported separately.
champion.note: The champion only speaks when its trigger fires; on most games it has no view at all (status NO_VIEW), which is not a PASS. Read the live number and the backtest number separately — they are far apart, and the live sample is small.

model_v4.label: V4 model grid
model_v4.what: The v4 model grid's best playable totals lean on the game (+EV gate at the real price AND at least 1 point of model-vs-market disagreement).

archive_asof_wall.what: as-of-wall reconstruction of a day the board WAS live (leak-safe two-pass recipe, hash-asserted); not a fresh backtest, but not the served row byte-for-byte either

live_ledger.what: the v4 grid's own live graded ledger — the rows the board served

model_v4.basis: POPULATION: every game where the v4 model grid had a playable totals row that settled — one row per game (core playable preferred over an expanded-band row, then highest score). This DELIBERATELY INCLUDES games the champion also played, which record.by_source.model does NOT: by_source counts only the games the model FILLED after the champion passed, so the two numbers differ and neither is wrong. GRADING: the grid's own graded rows — as-of-wall archive where a day has one, else the live graded ledger — at each row's real executable per-side price. HEADLINE COVERS: 2026-07-06 forward (the first day the grid's live ledger graded anything).
model_v4.note: The grid rates every game, so it has a view on almost everything. Most of those views are PASSes; the bet set is the playable rows only. Its record here is bigger than record.by_source.model because this counts every game it played, not only the ones it filled.

expanded_band.label: Expanded band
expanded_band.what: The narrow near-miss band: full +EV gate cleared but the model/market disagreement is only 0.75-1.0 points. Live from 2026-07-24, stakes 0.5u, graded on its own.

live_ledger.what: the v4 grid's own live graded ledger — the rows the board served

backtest.window: 2026-03-25..2026-07-23 (walk-forward rows only; one game per day-game, best-EV wall; graded vs settled finals at the row's own executable price)

simulator.label: Physical run simulator
simulator.what: A fully-physical Monte Carlo of the game — every plate appearance drawn from empirical base-out transition tables tilted to the two lineups, starters, bullpens, park, weather and umpire as of each decision wall (T-24h through T-1h, re-priced as inputs firm up, each wall written once), with home-field advantage on, 20,000 games simulated — priced into P(over the posted total). The lean that grades is the latest wall locked at first pitch. Shown for transparency: on full-game totals it statistically TIES the market (its median lands within ~0.02 runs of the posted line; blend-vs-market p=0.28), so it is a tracked voice, never a bet.

record.by_strategy_note: READ THIS BEFORE COMPARING STRATEGIES. (1) THEY OVERLAP: the same game appears in more than one stream — expanded_band is a strict SUBSET of model_v4, and unified is whichever of champion/model_v4 won that game. Their records are NOT additive: do not sum n, units or ROI across strategies, and do not read 'four strategies' as four independent bets. (2) NO POST-HOC PICKING: choosing whichever stream currently looks best is not a strategy — with four overlapping streams on a few dozen graded picks, one of them looks good by construction. The only number that ever described a real bankroll is the served unified pick from its activation date forward. (3) LIVE vs BACKTEST are kept apart on purpose: each strategy's headline n/W-L-P here is its LIVE-SERVED picks only; reconstructed / walk-forward / would-have measurements sit in `backtest`, are labeled, and are never added to the live number. `combined_view` restates the union ONLY because the older published blocks (record.overall, record.by_source) report it — it is not a live record. There is no staked-versus-lean split any more: every analyst is scored the same way, on its own reads, one row per game, and the sample size is printed beside the rate. Nothing here is a bet, nothing here sizes a bet, and nothing here touches the served product pick or the champion product record.
analysts.honest_note: WHAT THIS RECORD CAN AND CANNOT SUPPORT. The four models were fitted on 2025-01-01 -> 2026-06-30 and the record starts the day after, so it is genuinely out of sample and the leakage audit proves the fence four ways. But it is still only a few hundred games per analyst: at n=330 the 95% interval on a hit rate is roughly +/-5.4 points, which is wider than any edge worth having. The STANDING HYGIENE RULE therefore applies in full — no model-performance conclusion is drawn from this record, in either direction, and a rate below 50% is no more a finding than a rate above it. What the re-architecture is actually for is DECORRELATION: the four now read disjoint features and their sides agree only about as often as coin flips would, which is what makes their disagreement worth rendering.

patterns.honest_note: THE PATTERN TABLE IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A BET RULE. Every row carries its n and an EXACT binomial (Clopper-Pearson) 95% interval; a hit rate whose interval straddles 50% is a coin flip no matter how far from 50% the point estimate looks, and a row is a FINDING only if it survives ONE Benjamini-Hochberg pass across the entire rendered family. REPOINTED 2026-07-31: the four sides come from the re-architected v2 analysts (analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date, the published chief contract) — SCOUT the arms, NOVA the bats, ATLAS the conditions, VEGA the price — not from the four ledgers of the previous analysts, which no longer exist. THE BUCKETS MOVED AND THAT IS NOT A RESULT: the re-architecture decorrelated the four deliberately, so they disagree far more (side agreement fell from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57) and all sixteen configurations now occur where most previously never did. Different population is not better or worse performance. The corpus restarts at 2026-07-01, the day after the training fence of 2026-06-30, so it is genuinely out of sample and genuinely small — it will stay small for months and the intervals say so. The two eras are computed and shown separately and are NEVER summed: `reconstructed_era` is the July slate priced after the fact by models fitted before it, `live_era` is reads served before the games were played. Betting confidence remains solely the champion EV gate + the star system — nothing in this table gates, sizes or creates a bet.

desk_calls.note: THE DESK'S CALLS, GRADED IN THEIR OWN LEDGER. This is NOT a betting record and must never be summed with one, shown beside one as a comparison, or described in units: a call has no price and no stake, so it has no ROI. It counts one row per game — the desk's view at the most informed wall it reached — and it exists to answer one question the product could not previously ask: when the desk says something, is it right? A CALL IS NOT A BET. This is the desk's directional view on the game — what it actually thinks — built from the four analysts' own reads, equal-weighted. It is NEVER staked, it NEVER enters games[].pick, it is never counted in the product record, and it cannot be sized. Whether we are betting this game is a separate question with a separate answer, at `we_are_betting` / `bet_action`, decided by the price gate alone and unchanged by anything here. The graded product remains games[].pick and only games[].pick; the desk's calls are graded in their own ledger, separately, from 2026-08-01.
desk_calls.honest_note: THE STANDING HYGIENE RULE APPLIES IN FULL. This ledger starts at 2026-08-01 and will take months to say anything. A hit rate here is not evidence of edge in either direction, and in particular a call that beats 50% is NOT an argument for loosening the price gate — the gate is what protects the product record and it does not move on this.
desk_calls.contract: THE DESK-CALL CONTRACT (2026-08-01). WHAT IT IS: a directional view on EVERY game — side, conviction, a probability and a one-line argument — built from the four analysts' own reads, equal-weighted (the measured house position: desk_fit's walk-forward refused a fitted combiner). SERVED AT games[].diamondedge.desk_call. WHAT IT IS NOT: A CALL IS NOT A BET. Whether we are betting a game is decided by the price gate alone and is served, unchanged, at games[].diamondedge.action (PLAY / LEAN / AVOID, where AVOID still means and only means that no bet was served) and at games[].pick. Every call row hard-stamps is_bet=False, staked=False, stake_units=None, playable=False, suggested_units=None, take=False, stars=None and pick_side=None, and those stamps are re-asserted on every write and every read; the module may write only its own three stores and refuses every served board and product ledger by name. THE VOCABULARY, and a reader can never mistake one axis for the other: `desk_call.call` is the CALL (STRONG/CLEAR/SLIGHT + OVER/UNDER), `desk_call.state` fuses both axes (CALL_AND_PLAY / CALL_AND_LEAN / CALL_NO_BET / CALL_NO_GAME / PENDING), `we_are_betting` is the bet in one boolean, and `why_no_bet` names the reason when it is false. GRADING: the graded product remains games[].pick and ONLY games[].pick. The desk's calls are graded in their own append-only ledger, one row per game at its most informed wall, from 2026-08-01, with no units and no ROI because a call has no price.

supplemental_serve.what_this_is: OWNER-DIRECTED SUPPLEMENTAL PICKS. Leon adds these by hand from the expanded nightly engine (v2). They FILL games the desk did not pick and never override one. They are served pregame at a real price, graded under the same outcome-verification gate as every other pick, and counted in the record under source 'engine_v2_owner'.
supplemental_serve.admission_rules: A supplemental row is REFUSED, never silently dropped and never quietly applied. The two admission rules are re-checked on every payload build: the game must have no served pick already, and it must still be pregame with 10 minutes of margin. Once a row has been admitted it is served from the write-once as-served ledger and the gate is not re-run — a served pick never un-serves itself.

withdrawals.what_this_is: OWNER-DIRECTED WITHDRAWAL. Leon superseded a still-PREGAME served pick with a newer engine's verdict, so the board serves that game as a PASS. Nothing was edited or deleted: the original row is archived verbatim in state/superseded_picks_<date>.jsonl alongside the supersession, its reason, its authorisation and its timestamp. A withdrawal is refused outright once the game is inside the 10-minute pregame margin — after first pitch, choosing which open bet to keep is exactly what a public record may never do. Because the game was never decided, it leaves the day's denominator rather than entering it as a loss or a win.
